column3: It directly joins the messenger's standing with being under the Lord's watchful care and worship.
Seeking refuge in the all-hearing, all-knowing God develops the protecting perception behind the focus.
Its warning to an unwarnered people does not clarify the divine seeing of the messenger's standing.
Forbidding a servant is a distant contrast to the protected act of rising before God.
The immediate warning against calling on another god frames the prophetic service observed in the focus.
Seeing punishment eventually corrects false allegiance, but not the focus's present observation of the messenger.
Regret on seeing punishment supplies only a future consequence of sight.
The direct command to rely on the Mighty, Merciful gives the posture of trust immediately before the focus.
The deniers' eventual sight of the threatened event is only a distant outcome parallel.
The criminals' despair when the Hour rises adds no specific light to divine observation of the messenger.
Truth overcoming the magicians' work is a remote counterpart to the focus's watched prophetic action.

The separation at the Hour is unrelated to the seen act of standing.
The command to warn the nearest kin specifies the prophetic task surrounding the focus.

Denial and turning away do not elucidate the focus.
The immediate continuation shows the messenger's movement among those prostrating under the same divine perception.
Prophetic warning to a previously unwarned people gives only a general mission context.
Turning away is too indeterminate to clarify the focus.
The defeated magicians' reversal is only a distant bodily contrast.

Creation and proportioning do not develop the observed standing.

Unseen divine forces aiding the messenger give a limited parallel to unseen divine support.
Divine dominion and loss at the Hour do not specify divine observation of the messenger.

A fixed period of enjoyment is only a temporal echo, with little added to the seen act of standing.
Dispute over the length of worldly stay does not clarify the focus.
The magicians falling prostrate offers a distant bodily resonance after the nearer prostration context.
It distinguishes truthful inward reception from what is seen, enriching the reliability of perception.
Moses entering at an unguarded time does not illuminate divine observation of standing.
The messenger's disavowal of disobedient deeds immediately precedes reliance and divine observation in this passage.
The summons concerning Pharaoh's people provides only a broad prophetic commissioning parallel.
The burden weighing on the messenger's back is not a meaningful parallel to the focus.
Just weighing belongs to another local channel and adds little to the focus's observed worshipful movement.
Noah's commission to warn his people is a general prophetic-mission parallel.
Looking from couches does not clarify the focus's divine sight.
A community standing in night recitation and prostration gives a substantive worship-posture parallel.
Seeing one's smallest evil deed is a judgment motif, not the divine observation of the messenger's action.
Death and revival in Abraham's praise do not develop the focus.
The descent of the trustworthy Spirit gives a limited revelation context but not the focus's watched standing.
Steadfast uprightness under God's sight closely parallels standing as accountable obedience.
Regular glorification at named times gives a meaningful temporal worship parallel to rising in praise.
The envoys' fear before Pharaoh supplies only broad mission-and-protection context.
Visible renewal of earth points to divine knowledge and power only indirectly.
Looking from couches remains unrelated to the focus.
The Lord's cosmic governance gives theological context but little specific help with the observed standing.
The absence of sun and cold in Paradise does not clarify the focus.
Teaching by the pen is a broad knowledge theme without the focus's relational observation.
God's assurance of being with the envoys as One who hears and sees directly parallels protective divine perception.
A report becoming known after a time gives only a limited temporal counterpart.
God showing signs invites remembrance but does not explain His seeing the messenger rise.
Pharaoh's threat after the magicians' belief does not clarify the focus.
The messenger's sight of great signs gives a significant but distinct prophetic vision parallel.
God's showing of lightning is a general display-of-signs motif only.
Remembrance while standing, sitting, and lying down closely develops embodied worship across postures and appointed time.
Faith in the unseen expressed through established prayer provides a meaningful worship context for the focus.
The beauty of livestock at their movements only shares a time expression.
Near regret after a delay supplies only a temporal consequence motif.
Leaving deniers for a time is a limited parallel to measured divine timing.
A servant praying is a close act-of-worship parallel, though it lacks the focus's divine seeing.
Pharaoh's people's arrogance is unrelated to the focus.
An unknown period of trial and enjoyment offers only a broad temporal relation.
A brief act of looking is too slight to add interpretive value.
Night spent in prostration and standing gives a close worship-posture counterpart.
A second vision is a distant parallel to the focus's divine, rather than human, sight.
The departing night does not clarify the focus.
Truthful recitation of God's signs gives a broad devotional context only.
Temporary earthly settlement after the fall provides only a general time motif.
Frequent glorification is related worship but adds little after stronger standing-and-praise cards.
Resurrection on the Day of Rising is not about the focus's standing act.

Arrogant night talk does not develop the focus.
The timing of disclosure concerns questions and revelation, not the messenger's observed action.

God's hearing and knowledge accompany communal change, but the link to the focus is general.
The repeated command to turn away for a time is largely redundant with the earlier parallel.
Noah's people's transgression does not clarify the focus.
The heavens and earth standing by God's command gives a broad theological use of standing.
Human existence over time does not illuminate divine observation of the messenger.
Showy worship is a contrast to worship practiced under God's true sight.

The elites' flawed judgment by appearances contrasts broadly with the Lord who truly sees.
The unbelievers' inability to ward off fire does not clarify the focus.
Seeing punishment exposes broken human ties, a distant consequence-of-sight parallel.
Fruit at every time gives only a temporal recurrence motif.

Repeated exposure to fire and the Hour's rising do not explain the focus.
The Day of Decision is too general to add value.
Darkness preventing sight contrasts generally with the clear divine perception in the focus.
People call on God sincerely in peril, a limited trust parallel without the focus's seeing motif.
The vision of punishment at death is a distant judgment counterpart.
The command to avoid other gods echoes the nearby warning but adds little after that direct context.
Created signs invite recognition of divine power, but not specifically His observation of prophetic standing.

Rejecting visible signs contrasts generally with the focus's assured divine sight.
The aftermath visible after destruction is a remote judgment-and-sight parallel.
Zechariah receives the announcement while standing in prayer, a direct prophetic standing-in-worship parallel.
The command to stand devoutly before God directly supplies the reverent posture implicit in the focus.
Remembering God while standing, sitting, and lying down closely parallels embodied, continuous devotion.
Night devotion in prostration and standing gives a close devotional counterpart to the focus and its next ayah.
The communal prayer scene joins standing watchfully with prostration, closely matching the focus passage's movement among worshippers.
The Prophet and his companions are visibly characterized by bowing and prostrating, a direct communal parallel to the following ayah.
The command to prostrate and draw near completes the prayer scene whose standing servant appears among the candidates.
The command to rise and warn closely joins standing with the messenger's commissioned service.
The additional night prayer presents a distinct mode of the messenger's devoted nocturnal service.
Praise before sunrise and sunset supplies a regular temporal frame for the standing worship in the focus.
Glorification after prostration directly complements the focus's movement among those prostrating.

The command to bow, prostrate, worship, and do good gives the wider embodied worship sequence around the focus.
Those who leave their beds to call on their Lord provide a close night-devotion parallel.
The angels near the Lord do not disdain His worship and prostrate before Him, extending the prostration motif.
Mary is commanded to devote herself, prostrate, and bow with the worshippers, a close posture-based parallel.
